sources.title: RIT CSCI-421 Principles of Database System Implementation catalog description
sources.author: Rochester Institute of Technology
sources.content: This course provides a broad introduction to database management systems including data modeling, the relational model, and SQL. Database system implementation issues are covered next, where the focus is on data structures and algorithms used to implement database management systems. Topics include physical data organization, indexing and hashing, query processing and optimization, database recovery techniques, transaction management, concurrency control, and database performance evaluation. A programming project will be required. Prerequisites: CSCI-320. Students may not take and receive credit for CSCI-421 and CSCI-621. If you have earned credit for CSCI-621 or you are currently enrolled in CSCI-621 you will not be permitted to enroll in CSCI-421. Contact Hours: Lecture 3 Typically Offered: Fall, Spring, Summer

sources.title: PostgreSQL Documentation
sources.author: PostgreSQL Global Development Group
sources.content: Relational systems organize data with tables, rows, columns, and declared types. Primary keys identify rows, while foreign keys express references between tables. Constraints reject states that violate declared data rules. Queries select, join, aggregate, insert, update, and delete data. Indexes provide additional access paths for selected queries. Transactions group operations into an atomic unit of work. Isolation controls how concurrent transactions observe one another. Schema design separates entities and relationships, while normalization addresses update anomalies. Query planning and physical structures influence performance without changing logical query meaning.

sources.title: Neo4j Graph Data Modeling
sources.author: Neo4j
sources.content: Property graph models represent domain entities as nodes. Relationships connect nodes and have a type and direction. Nodes and relationships can carry properties. Labels group nodes that play a similar domain role. A useful graph model begins from the questions the application must answer. Traversal patterns determine which relationships the application follows. Identity must be explicit when several records may describe the same entity. Constraints and indexes support data integrity and efficient lookup. Direction, cardinality, and update behavior are part of the model.
